# usePolling

> Poll on an interval without overlapping requests, pausing while the tab is hidden.

🟡 intermediate · React 18.0+ · Custom Hooks › Data fetching & async · support: client-only

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-polling`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-polling)

## Concept

A `setTimeout` chain: poll, wait for it to settle, then schedule the next one `intervalMs` later. Document visibility is read with `useSyncExternalStore`; hiding the page tears the loop down, showing it starts with an immediate poll.

## Problem

`setInterval(fetch, 2000)` overlaps requests when the server is slow, keeps hammering the API from background tabs, and leaks if not cleared.

## When to use

- Dashboards and status pages where seconds-old data is acceptable and no push channel exists.

## When not to use

- When the server can push — use `useWebSocket` or `useSSE`.
- Production server state — TanStack Query `refetchInterval` (+ `refetchIntervalInBackground`) and SWR `refreshInterval` do this with caching.

## API

```ts
function usePolling<T>(
  fn: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>,
  options: { intervalMs: number; enabled?: boolean; pauseWhenHidden?: boolean },
): {
  data: T | undefined;
  error: Error | undefined;
  isFetching: boolean;
  isPaused: boolean;
  updatedAt: number | undefined;
  refresh: () => void;
};
```

| Parameter                      | Type                     | Description                                                |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fn`                           | `(signal) => Promise<T>` | Latest function is used.                                   |
| `intervalMs`                   | `number`                 | Gap between the end of one poll and the start of the next. |
| `enabled` _(optional)_         | `boolean`                | Default `true`.                                            |
| `pauseWhenHidden` _(optional)_ | `boolean`                | Default `true`.                                            |

**Returns:** Latest data (kept on errors), last error, flags, `updatedAt` and a stable `refresh()`.

## Execution flow

1. Effect (active = enabled and visible): schedules the first poll, then each next poll after the previous settles.
2. Cleanup (hidden, disabled, interval change, `refresh`, unmount): clears the timer and aborts the request in flight.

## Common mistakes

### setInterval with async work

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(async () => setStats(await getStats()), 2000);
  return () => clearInterval(id);
}, []);
```

If a request takes longer than 2 s, requests pile up and responses may arrive out of order; it also polls from hidden tabs.

## Edge cases

- A failing poll keeps the last good `data` and keeps polling.
- Returning to the tab polls immediately, so the data is never older than one interval after focus.

## Browser support

Idle on the server.

## Testing

Fake-timer tests prove no overlap with a slow response, interval timing, error handling, pause/resume via `setDocumentVisibility`, `refresh` aborting the request, and cleanup on disable/unmount (`vi.getTimerCount() === 0`).

## Production considerations

- Back off the interval on repeated errors and stop polling for logged-out users.
